harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway for the private "lan" network (10.50.50.0/24, egress:false) so node2 and node3 can reach the internet through it, implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the designated control_node (node4). node1's eth1 got a static LAN address (10.50.50.1/24) plus a masquerade source-NAT rule out eth0; node2/node3's enp8s0 got static LAN addresses and a low-priority (metric 200) default route via node1, leaving their existing mgmt-network default route (metric 100) untouched so management/exec access was never disrupted. Diagnosed and fixed a strict rp_filter drop on the LAN interfaces that was silently discarding de-NATed return traffic (classic asymmetric-route RPF issue). Verified end-to-end egress from node2/node3 via the private interface specifically (HTTP 204 from a live internet endpoint), confirmed idempotent playbook re-runs, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four managed nodes with boot-id-verified restarts and full post-restart recovery — including fixing a VyOS SSH-key reconciler issue where the login config (not just the authorized_keys file) must hold the cluster SSH key or it gets wiped on every boot.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: mgmt network (dhcp+egress) and lan network (no dhcp, no egress) connecting node1+node2+node3; confirmed control_node=node4 from environment.toml
Set up passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user), node2 and node3 (root) using the cluster-provided SSH keypair

Wrote and ran an Ansible playbook (inventory.ini + nat-egress.yml on node4) configuring VyOS eth1 static IP + NAT masquerade source rule via VyOS configure/commit/save, and node2/node3 enp8s0 static IPs via nmcli with a low-priority default route via node1

Diagnosed a return-traffic drop via tcpdump on node1's eth0/eth1 (showed NAT working correctly) vs a failing ping on node2; root-caused to strict rp_filter on enp8s0 and fixed with ansible.posix.sysctl, persisted to /etc/sysctl.conf
Verified egress from node2 and node3 specifically via the private LAN interface (curl --interface enp8s0) returning HTTP 204 from an internet endpoint
Re-ran the playbook to confirm idempotency
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, interface/route state, NAT config, live egress test) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node2, node3, node1, then node4 one at a time via native reboot, polling each until exec access returned and confirming boot_id changed each time

After node1's reboot, found VyOS's system_login.py reconciler had wiped the manually-added authorized_keys entry; fixed by adding the SSH key through VyOS's own 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' config so it survives reboots

Re-verified NAT config, static IPs, rp_filter settings, and live internet egress from node2/node3 through node1 after all restarts, and confirmed node4's Ansible control access and playbook idempotency post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 provides NAT for node2/node3 on the private lan network via Ansible
evidence.summary: ansible-playbook run from control_node node4 against inventory of node1 (router) and node2/node3 (lan_clients) applies VyOS static LAN IP + NAT masquerade rule and client static IPs/routes; final run shows node2 and node3 returning HTTP 204 via the private enp8s0 interface

evidence.requirement: NAT actually forwards traffic correctly (not just config present)
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's eth0 (WAN) and eth1 (LAN) simultaneously while pinging from node2 shows correct masquerade translation both directions (10.50.50.11 <-> 10.100.177.10 <-> 1.1.1.1), proving live NAT forwarding

evidence.requirement: Root cause and fix of return-path drop (rp_filter)
evidence.summary: Identified rp_filter=1 on enp8s0 as the cause of silent return-packet drops; fixed via sysctl and confirmed persisted to /etc/sysctl.conf
SSH/exec access to all nodes via mgmt network verified working before and after all changes; mgmt default route (metric 100) left untouched, lan route added only as metric 200 secondary path

evidence.requirement: node2 baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5161af9e.../rp_filter=2/HTTP 204 captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 9fc48d24... after poll; post-restart shows interface, route, rp_filter and live internet egress all recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9feeb0bb.../rp_filter=2/HTTP 204 captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to d999b006... after poll; post-restart shows interface, route, rp_filter and live internet egress all recovered

evidence.requirement: node1 (router) baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5bcff8f9.../eth1 IP/NAT config captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to f216192b... after poll; post-restart shows eth1 IP and ip_forward recovered, and node2+node3 both get live internet egress (HTTP 204) through node1 again

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d3d54083... and Ansible ping captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 5adb35e9... after poll; post-restart Ansible connectivity to all managed nodes and a full idempotent playbook re-run both succeeded

evidence.requirement: VyOS SSH-key reconciler issue found and fixed (needed for node1 restart recovery)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot SSH to node1 failed because VyOS's system_login.py regenerated authorized_keys from its own config, discarding the manually-added key; fixed by adding the key via 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' + commit/save, after which Ansible connectivity to node1 was restored
